newsitem.title: FRANCE: French magazines for men draw strong ad spending.
newsitem.headline: French magazines for men draw strong ad spending.

text.p: Advertising in French men's magazines jumped 36.4 percent rise in value in the first four months of this year compared with a year earlier, magazine Carat Medias Actualites said on Thursday.

The men's magazines seemed to benefit from a transfer of advertising from car magazines, where advertising spending was depressed in line with a slump in the car sector, said the magazine, which is owned by advertising agency Carat, and draws on information from Carat's measurement arm, Carat Expert.

Overall the French press saw advertising receipts rise 9.2 percent in the four months to the end of April compared with 1996's first four months, putting total advertising spending in the sector above seven billion francs, the magazine said.
"This new spring time which daily newspapers and magazines are experiencing is developing in a fairly favourable market context," Carat Medias Actualites said.

Forecasts for the French advertising market this year have varied after a slowdown in the sector, particularly in newspapers, magazines and posters, but most analysts expect some sort of recovery this year.
Daily newspapers saw advertising receipts rise 10.5 percent in 1997's first four months, while advertising receipts at all categories of magazines rose 8.5 percent, Carat Medias Actualites said.
Receipts at women's magazines, which represent a fifth of the French press and magazine sector, were up 18.5 percent in the period, giving a total spend of 989 million francs.

The rise in women's magazines' advertising receipts, more marked among specialists in decoration, family and parenting or gossip, comes despite a 1.6 percent slide in circulation in the sector last year. Carat Media Actualites did not say which women's magazines had suffered the biggest circulation falls.

Magazines for children and teenagers saw a 33 percent rise in advertising receipts, while receipts at television magazines, which represent 40 percent of France's general magazines, rose 9.7 percent, barely above the average, it said.
